Optimal.Notes: A stable 40 fps cap at 40 Hz gives smooth combat in Story mode with a reasonable balance of visual quality and battery life. GE-Proton is recommended by the community for better Ubisoft Connect compatibility.

profiles.Summary: For Honor runs in Story/offline modes under Proton but EasyAntiCheat blocks all online multiplayer on Linux, severely limiting the experience. The Deck's GPU sits at the minimum spec class, so 30–40 fps is achievable at low settings in the playable offline content.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum requirements and Deck hardware class. On first run, check frame rate during combat and fall back to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if it dips below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and use Deck FSR to upscale to 1280x800, keeping TDP low for extended sessions. Only Story mode is accessible due to EAC blocking online play.

KnownIssues: EasyAntiCheat blocks all online multiplayer (4v4, 2v2, 1v1 PvP and Co-op) on Linux — only Story mode and offline bots are accessible
Denuvo DRM may cause stutters or slow startup on first launch or after game updates

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with medium settings the Deck can approach 60 fps in lighter scenes but will dip to 40-45 fps in busier combat; expect inconsistency. Drop to Optimal profile if stutters are noticeable.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap provides smooth, tear-free gameplay that suits For Honor's melee combat pacing. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers visual clarity at a manageable power cost.

profiles.Summary: For Honor is a 2017 melee PvP action game whose PC minimum GPU (GTX 950/R9 270) sits just below the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU class, suggesting it can run at 30–45 fps with low-to-medium settings. The game uses EasyAntiCheat and Denuvo, which can cause compatibility issues under Proton — online multiplayer may not function, but single-player and some modes may work.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs versus Steam Deck hardware. On first launch, check frame rate in a busy 4v4 match — if it dips below 30, switch to Max Battery settings and lower texture quality further. Also verify whether online modes function under Proton/EAC before investing time.

MaxBattery.Notes: GE-Proton is recommended for better EAC and Denuvo compatibility. Dropping to a sub-native render resolution with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU well within the TDP budget for extended sessions.

KnownIssues: EasyAntiCheat (EAC) may block online multiplayer under Proton — online PvP and co-op modes may be unavailable or unstable.
Denuvo anti-tamper technology can cause stuttering or slow loading on first launch under Proton.
No official controller support listed; partial controller support may require remapping for full playability.
Game is Steam Deck 'Unsupported' — some UI elements and menus may not scale well to the 1280x800 display.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full TDP and native resolution, the Deck can approach 60 fps in less demanding scenes but may dip to the mid-40s in busy 4v4 fights — consider dropping to 45 fps cap if stutters occur. Battery life will be short at this setting.
